Automated Model Briefing

⚠ AI-generated text — may be wrong, incomplete, or overconfident. This is automated commentary on experimental model output, not flight advice and not a weather forecast. It has not been reviewed by a meteorologist.

Overall Assessment A good thermal soaring day with light surface winds, moderate climb rates, and no precipitation. Lapse rates are sharp (9.3–10.0 °C/km site-wide), demanding advanced pilot skills. High cloud bases and deep boundary layers support extended XC flights, but thermal turbulence will be punchy and low-level shear exists at a few sites.

Site Breakdown

  • Kingsbury grade: Marginal — light crosswind from N during peak thermal hours, but still flyable. Flying window 9am–4pm. Peak w* 346 ft/min, thermal ceiling 5219 ft AGL. Sharp thermals (advanced pilots only).
  • Hallelujah: Favorable — onshore W–NW flow aligns well with launch; good ridge soaring potential. Flying window 10:30am–5pm. Peak w* 427 ft/min, thermal ceiling 5934 ft AGL. Sharp thermals; watch for directional shear (peak 37°).
  • Slide Mountain: Favorable — S–SE winds directly on launch, light and steady. Flying window 8:30am–3pm (thermals end by 4pm). Peak w* 335 ft/min, thermal ceiling 2538 ft AGL. Sharp thermals.
  • McClellan: Favorable — light SE–S winds, excellent for thermal flying with prime conditions after 12:30pm. Flying window 10am–6pm. Peak w* 473 ft/min, thermal ceiling 6231 ft AGL. Sharp thermals.
  • West McClellan: Favorable — light, variable flow becoming NW later, suitable for multiple launch directions. Flying window 10am–6pm. Peak w* 435 ft/min, thermal ceiling 5223 ft AGL. Sharp thermals.
  • Peavine Mountain: Favorable — S–SE winds early, light throughout the thermal window. Flying window 9am–4pm. Peak w* 388 ft/min, thermal ceiling 3745 ft AGL. Sharp thermals.
  • Rainbow Ridge: Favorable — easterly flow directly up the ridge, strong thermal heights and good ridge soaring. Flying window 9am–5pm, prime after 1pm. Peak w* 428 ft/min, thermal ceiling 7296 ft AGL. Sharp thermals; note hazardous low-level speed shear (5 mph) and directional shear (36°).
  • Duck Hill: Marginal — crosswind in the morning (SE), but turns NW onshore by mid-afternoon, favoring the launch. Thermal flying possible from late morning. Flying window ~11am–6pm. Peak w* 419 ft/min, thermal ceiling 7021 ft AGL. Sharp thermals.
  • Daydreams: Unfavorable — no thermal activity predicted; wind direction not aligned for ridge soaring. Not flyable today.

Hazards

  • Sharp, punchy thermals — Lapse rates 9.3–10.0 °C/km at all sites; suitable only for advanced/expert pilots.
  • Low-level directional shear — Hallelujah (37°) and Rainbow Ridge (36°); can create rough, broken lift near the top of the boundary layer.
  • Low-level speed shear — Rainbow Ridge (5 mph at 7,587 ft AGL); abrupt wind changes possible.
  • Rotor/lee turbulence — Downwind of Peavine Mountain and the Carson Range ridgelines when winds are S/SE, veering E in the afternoon; avoid lee-side areas.
  • No icing, precipitation, or overdevelopment — Freezing level ~15,600 ft MSL remains well above maximum thermal ceilings.

Site Forecast ?Top of Thermals (PBLH) — height of the turbulent mixing layer; thermals typically reach this ceiling.
LCL (Lifted Condensation Level) — altitude where rising air reaches its dew point; theoretical cloud base.
Cloud Base — lowest model level with >10% cloud fraction.
w* — convective velocity scale; higher = stronger thermals (ft/min).
Cloud Cover — max cloud fraction over the column (0–100%).
Wind thresholds: orange = 12 mph, red = 18 mph.
